title: LoRAHub composition over a Mirror-compressed candidate basis
hypothesis: For a candidate LoRA bank whose full functional updates lie on a shared rank-2 Givens orbit, per-candidate Mirror angles can preserve LoRAHub few-shot signed-composition quality with no more than 60% of the independent candidate-bank payload, while scalar gates cannot recover that quality.
physical_object: Eight frozen rank-2 LoRA candidate modules mapping 16D frozen features to 16D residual outputs, followed by four target-task signed scalar compositions selected from few-shot support data.
mirror_coordinate: One per-candidate SO(2) Givens angle inserted between a shared rank-2 LoRA input factor A and output factor B; target LoRAHub composition coefficients remain the same independently optimized signed scalars for all bank variants.
logical_multiplicity: Eight source LoRA functions and four few-shot target compositions over their bank.
prior_art_delta: PA55/LoraHub freezes multiple candidate LoRA modules and learns positive/negative scalar composition weights on a few-shot target task. This experiment keeps that target-side scalar search unchanged and compresses only the source candidate bank.

methods: independent rank-2 LoRA candidate bank + signed LoRAHub coefficients
one hard-tied LoRA candidate + signed coefficients
shared rank-2 basis + scalar source gates + signed coefficients
shared rank-2 basis + unrestricted 2x2 per-candidate coefficients + signed coefficients
shared rank-2 basis + one Givens angle per candidate + signed coefficients
model.source_schedule: Every update uses the same sampled 64 feature vectors for all eight candidate source tasks; mean source-bank MSE is minimized. Freeze each source bank before target composition adaptation.
model.target_schedule: For each of four target tasks, train an 8-value signed coefficient vector on the same 64 support examples for all methods, 300 Adam updates. Evaluate once on 2,048 held-out features.

teacher.source_update: B0 @ R(theta_i) @ A0, where B0 and A0 are shared within each world and each R is one SO(2) rotation. This is an explicitly aligned feasibility fixture.
teacher.target_task: Sparse signed mixture of three source candidate outputs; fixed target coefficients are generated before adaptation and are not exposed to any method.
teacher.data: Independent Gaussian frozen-feature examples; source and target outputs are deterministic linear functions of the features.

controls: full independently parameterized rank-2 LoRA candidate bank, mandatory LoRAHub upper/storage control
shared basis with scalar source gates
shared basis with unrestricted per-candidate 2x2 coefficient matrices
shared basis with per-candidate Givens angles
identical signed target-coefficient adaptation for every method

development.selection_metric: mean target-test NRMSE over four target tasks; also report source candidate NRMSE, support fit, actual total payload bytes and composition search compute
development.allowed_tuning: No hyperparameter search; fixed architecture and training schedule are run once. Any implementation correction must rerun development before fresh access.

fresh.open_gate: Both development worlds: full independent source-bank NRMSE <=0.03; Mirror target-test NRMSE <= independent-bank +0.01 and <=0.05; Mirror total payload <=0.60x independent; Mirror improves target-test NRMSE over scalar gates by >=0.01 at <=1.10x scalar bytes; unrestricted 2x2 coefficients do not match Mirror within 0.005 NRMSE at <=Mirror bytes; gauge audit max function-output delta <=1e-6. Otherwise fresh remains sealed.

storage.authority: actual serialized NPZ inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: all independent or shared LoRA A/B factors
all per-candidate Mirror angles, scalar gates, or 2x2 coefficient matrices
all four target-task signed LoRAHub composition vectors
dimensions, method tags, reconstruction metadata and NPZ names/headers/compression overhead

symmetry_audit.operation: For every independent candidate, apply a nonsingular non-orthogonal 2x2 gauge G: B'=B@G and A'=inv(G)@A. Compare full D=B@A and source/target predictions; a gauge-only transformation is not additional multiplicity.

success_gate: All three fresh worlds meet the source, target quality, <=60% total-payload, scalar-control and generic-coefficient gates; gauge audit and serialized metric replay pass.
failure_gate: Mirror fails the <=60% payload or quality gate, scalar control matches its useful quality at comparable bytes, generic 2x2 coordinates match within 0.005 NRMSE at no greater bytes, or gauge audit fails.
boundaries: aligned synthetic frozen-feature LoRA/LoRAHub feasibility proxy; no pretrained language model claim
source candidate bank is intentionally on a common rotation orbit; fresh results still do not establish natural-task compressibility
LoRA factor matrices are non-unique; compare full functional updates and logits/predictions, not raw factor similarity
few-shot composition is distinct from independently trained target adapters
fixed optimizer budget is not a near-converged capacity claim
